input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights." That is squarely the playbook's walk-away position: a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or exit, and it fails the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty). It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and sits uneasily with Section 7.1's bar on unidentified minimum-use charges. Redline replaces the commitment with the preferred position (payment for Services ordered or used only); the fallback 12-month reducible commitment with a true-up is offered in the comment if a commitment is commercially required.

proposal.summary: Replace three-year take-or-pay minimum with no minimum commitment; fees payable for ordered/used Services only
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced Section 2.1 with our standard position that fees are payable only for Services ordered or used. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss limiting it to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty. This also removes the conflict with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment.

ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: 2.1 Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment. Customer is obligated to pay only for Services ordered under an Order Form or actually used, and no shortfall, unused-capacity, or similar charge applies.
